rv.q: From the moment that the huge chandelier went careening from the stage up onto the ceiling as that organ riff played, I was hooked on the high-camp melodrama.
No room to interrogate his status as an abusive incel here, just a good yarn.
It is a powerful moment and it exemplifies the consistent delight in theatricality.
The Phantom of the Opera’s sheer theatrical verve is also immensely satisfying.
Lent a hand by Lloyd Webber’s sumptuous tunes, so too does this Phantom.
The show has only grown in its artistic power, the music swooping down from the gods to give you a glorious emotional rinsing.
'Phantom' remains strong because its high production values haven't been allowed to sag
There's no question that it's still wild, it's still joyous, and it's still deserved of its place as the pride of the West End
What is undeniable is that this show delivers world-class staging, music and performances.

On the strength of its slightly refreshed incarnation, this delicately reconstructed Phantom of the Opera looks set to be just as much a theatreland fixture as it was in its first three and a half decades.
For many, many years I have been a huge admirer of the maintenance of world-wide production standards but is less more?
The cast were all wonderful with Killian Donnelly showing his diverse acting and singing talent

cn.t: Lloyd Webber's gothic spectacular remains a crowd-pleaser after 35 years, with critics praising its infectious melodies, lavish staging, and unapologetically '80s spectacle that puts story first—even if it's deeply uncool.

ru.inst: Released daily at 10 AM via show website. Open Run.
